                    # post-restore pattern was fragile because callees could
                    # re-enable set -e mid-stream — observed in run_id
                    # 20260608223447-42915 where pipeline.abort fired between
                    # cycle.complete and where cycle.unconverged should have emitted.)
                    cycle_orchestrator_run "$_cyc_id" "$state_dir" "$state_file" && _rc=0 || _rc=$?
                    unset ZBUILD_SEQ_PREFIX
                    _runner_rearm_traps
                    _cycle_handle_terminal "$_cyc_id" "$state_file" || true
                    # #1850 (ADR-054 §4): how the loop ended is a word, never the rc.
                    local _cyc_outcome="${_CYCLE_LAST_OUTCOME:-}"

                    #               sigint/sigterm/cycle_abort → interrupted;
                    #               llm_unavailable/llm_rate_limited/scope_too_large

                        _RUNNER_CYCLE_UNCONVERGED_REASON="$_CYCLE_LAST_TERMINATED_REASON"
                        _RUNNER_CYCLE_UNCONVERGED_ID="$_cyc_id"

                        # final-status aggregator. _TPL_CYCLE_ON_MAX_<id> is
                        # populated by the template parser.

                        # failure (typically `test`) so review's `_review_derive_test_status`

                            "iter=${_CYCLE_LAST_ITERATIONS:-0}" \
                            "reason=$_CYCLE_LAST_TERMINATED_REASON" \
                            "run_id=$_runner_run_id" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
                            2>/dev/null || true

                        # #2241: `on_max: halt` STOPS the run here. Until now every
                        # unconverged cycle fell through to the next unit and halt
                        # only changed the final label — #1842's design never passed

                        # word runner-final-status used; it means the same.

                                    "reason=$_CYCLE_LAST_TERMINATED_REASON" "on_max=halt" \
                                    "run_id=$_runner_run_id" "issue=$_runner_issue" 2>/dev/null || true

                                    _verdict_resolve_path_v _du_resolved \

    local _DETECTED_PLATFORMS=()
    while IFS= read -r p; do
        [[ -n "$p" ]] && _DETECTED_PLATFORMS+=("$p")
    done < <(detect_platforms "$PWD" "$state_dir" 2>/dev/null)
    [[ ${#_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]} -eq 0 ]] && _DETECTED_PLATFORMS=("generic")

    if $resume_mode; then
        # ADR-025 (Wave 15-E #685): defensive sentinel cleanup at resume entry.
        # The normal SIGINT path's EXIT trap already disarms the sentinel
        # in `_runner_abort_trap`, but a hard kill (-9), host crash, or any
        # path that skipped the EXIT trap can leave a stale .abort.signal.
        # Without this disarm the first `_zbuild_check_abort` pre-flight in
        # the dispatch loop would observe the stale sentinel and abort the
        # resumed run immediately. Resume must always start from a clean
        # signal channel.
        _zbuild_disarm_abort_sentinel
        # ADR-006 §3.6 (#1805): restore completed-stage artifacts from the git
        # state branch before the dispatch loop, so complete stages have their
        # primary artifacts available. A still-absent artifact causes exit 1 at
        # the dispatch loop's stale-artifact check.
        _runner_resume_rehydrate "$_runner_issue" "$state_dir"
        # ADR-006 §3.6 (#1805): signal to cycle orchestrators that this is a
        # resume so they restore iteration count from state (SPEC-7).
        export _ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE=true
        eb_emit_event "pipeline.resume" "run_id=$_runner_run_id" "issue=$_runner_issue"
        info "Pipeline resuming — run_id=$_runner_run_id issue=${issue:-} goal=${goal:-} template=$template"
        if [[ -n "$from_stage" ]]; then
            warn "Skipping ahead to stage '$from_stage' as requested (--from-stage)"
            eb_emit_event "pipeline.skip_to_stage" "stage=$from_stage" "run_id=$_runner_run_id"
            # DSFSTG-1 (#1805): --from-stage restarts the target cycle from iter=1.
            # Clear the resume flag so the cycle orchestrator does not restore the
            # persisted iteration count — from-stage always starts the cycle fresh.
            export _ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE=false
            # DSFSTG-1 (#1805): when the from-stage target is a cycle, signal the cycle
            # orchestrator to emit stage.start for the first cycle member (iter=1 always).
            # Only set for cycle targets; leaf targets emit stage.start via the dispatch loop.
            # _ZBUILD_FROM_STAGE_EMIT_START is consumed by the first cycle orchestrator entry.
            if declare -p _TPL_CYCLES >/dev/null 2>&1; then
